The species was named in 1932 by paleontologist Charles Mook. "G. browni" has a longer snout with more teeth than "Dollosuchus", but it is not as long and does not have as many teeth as that of the gharial.  "G. browni" has also been proposed to be moved to a genus other than "Gavialis".
